key_insight: SpatialEvo leverages deterministic geometric environments to generate verifiable geometry signals for self-training, avoiding the consensus-driven error reinforcement of prior self-evolving methods. This enables models to self-improve on 3D spatial tasks using environment-derived ground-truth-like supervision.
problem_solved: Reduces reliance on costly manual 3D geometric annotation and prevents self-training from amplifying the model's own spatial errors caused by consensus-based pseudo-labeling.
method: Embed the agent/model in controllable, deterministic 3D geometric environments that yield predictable, verifiable spatial relationships.
Derive pseudo-labels from environment-determined geometric constraints (closed-form transforms / constraint checks) instead of model consensus, then use them to fine-tune the model iteratively.
Apply an iterative self-evolving loop with environment-based validation and selective acceptance to correct errors and progressively improve spatial reasoning.
impact: Enables continuous, low-cost improvement of 3D spatial reasoning models with less manual annotation and greater resistance to self-reinforced errors—beneficial for embodied AI, robotics, and 3D perception pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: deterministic 3D environment → geometry constraint engine → pseudo-labels → model fine-tuning (loop).

paper_title: SpatialEvo: Self-Evolving Spatial Intelligence via Deterministic Geometric Environments
paper_authors: Dinging Li, Yingxiu Zhao, Xinrui Cheng, Kangheng Lin, Hongbo Peng
